title: Why am I learning this: one link to valuing a company, from a story
source: Percent Session of 11 November 2026, turn 2 at Your turn (spec 2026-11-12, Part A Evidence, A6 and H6)
message: Why am I learning basis points? How does this connect to valuing a stock?

phrases: A basis point is a smaller ruler

graderChecks: Does it link basis points to valuing a company in one or two sentences, in its own words: through the Topic's "why it matters" line when the Topic has one, otherwise through one lever of a valuation story (how big the business gets, what it keeps, what growth costs, or how risky it is, such as the rate used to discount its future cash)?
Does it avoid saying or implying that a valuation starts from a rate? A valuation starts from a story about the business.
Does it then return to the step, without a lecture on valuation?
notes: Pass when (3 of 3 runs): a normal reply; 120 words or fewer; no sum asked; never "Valuing a company ... starts from a rate" (what the Learner got on 11 November, which H6 corrects: a valuation starts from a story about the business); and the grader finds one link to valuing a company in the Tutor's own words. A6 gives every Topic file a "why" line of 30 words or fewer that the Course Navigator message passes on; until Percent's file has one, the Tutor links the idea to one lever of a valuation story, as its instructions say.
